A furniture system that transforms. Metis takes its name from the Greek goddess of wisdom and adaptability: an entity whose defining quality is the capacity to change form without losing identity. The system does the same.

The idea

Contemporary spaces demand furniture that can keep up with how people actually live — not fixed objects for fixed behaviours, but elements that shift with the moment. Metis is a modular seating system designed to adapt naturally to any need, transform over time, and remain coherent across every context and style.

Essential in form. Born to transform.

Total modularity
Every element integrates with the others simply and reliably, guaranteeing adaptability in any context. Modules can be recombined, extended, or used independently.
Quick assembly
A few gestures are enough to radically change the configuration. No tools, no permanent decisions — the system responds to the moment.
Multiple functions
Lounge chair, coffee table, footrest. Three distinct functional identities from a single modular base. The same components read differently depending on how they are assembled.
Brand coherence
Geometry derived directly from the Sofable logo: two distinct sections of the mark informed the soft lines of the cushion and the structural logic of the base, binding the product to the brand at the level of form.

The forms

The geometry of Metis was not invented but extracted. Two distinct sections of the Sofable logo were isolated: the first inspired the soft, welcoming curves of the upholstered cushion elements; the second guided the design of the structural base, giving the whole system a visual and brand coherence that runs through every configuration.

The design process moved through hand sketches of module arrangements, structural diagrams, and 3D models of each configuration — each configuration derived from a functional logic rather than invented as a decorative variant.

The sketches trace the evolution from an initial block concept through structural and material explorations — wood, aluminium — to the final modular logic. The Sofable logo sections are annotated directly on the forms, making the brand derivation explicit at every stage of the process.

The three configurations

Each configuration gives the same base modules a different functional identity. The transition between them requires no tools — only the repositioning of the cushion elements and the reorientation of the base.

Lounge chair

The primary configuration. Both cushion modules sit upright within the base frame — a seat and a backrest — forming a reclined lounge chair suited to reading, resting, or watching. The curved wooden base cradles the sitter at a low, relaxed angle.

Form
Reclined · low seat · backrest
Use
Reading · resting · television

Footrest

The cushion modules are laid flat and stacked within the base, creating a low, cloud-like platform. Used as a footrest alongside the lounge chair configuration, or as a standalone pouf for occasional seating. The upholstered surface remains fully exposed.

Form
Low platform · cushion exposed
Use
Footrest · pouf · occasional seat

Table

The cushions are removed and the wooden base panel faces upward, presenting a flat lacquered surface. Magnetic elements integrated into the panel allow wireless device support. The base becomes a low living-room table suited to the same low height as the lounge configuration alongside it.

Form
Flat surface · magnetic panel
Use
Coffee table · device support

The base

The base was conceived to work actively on perspectival perception: the form derived from the Sofable logo reveals itself fully only from specific viewing angles, generating a dynamic visual effect. This allows a graphic reference to the brand to be embedded in the structure without compromising its load-bearing function.

The support points were carefully studied to guarantee stability, optimal weight distribution, and adaptability across the three configurations. The result is a structural element that combines load-bearing function, formal balance, and symbolic meaning — it is at once a leg, a logo, and a frame.

The cushion

The upholstered element is the system’s most engineered component. Its construction layers are designed to work together precisely:

Microfibre / cotton cover
Fully removable for easy cleaning and colour swapping. Available in two material categories — cotton and water-resistant microfibre — each in a curated palette drawn from the wider Sofable collection.
Shaped internal padding
Contoured padding with defined profiles, designed to fit precisely against the internal structure and maintain surface alignment during use across all configurations.
Clear-lacquered wooden panel
The structural base layer of the cushion. Integrated magnetic elements allow secure cover attachment and, when the table configuration is used, provide magnetic support for mobile devices on the exposed panel surface.
Laminated aluminium joinery
The structural connector that locks the two cushion modules together and slots into the base frame. It both enables the interlocking of the system and increases comfort when the two cushions are assembled into the lounge chair configuration.

Colours and materials

Starting from a complete analysis of the materials present in the Sofable collection, a chromatic selection was defined drawing on the brand’s most iconic models — including Boboli — and articulated across two material categories that together cover every use context, from domestic interiors to more exposed or outdoor-adjacent settings.

Cotton
Microfibre / water-resistant microfibre
The cover is fully interchangeable — swapping the colour or material of an existing Metis requires only removing the old cover and fitting the new one. The system's aesthetic identity can evolve without replacing any structural component.

A family of products in one

Just as a single configuration emerges from the combination of modules, the same principle scales outward. Multiple units of Metis can coexist in the same space in different configurations — one as a lounge chair, one as a table, one as a footrest — each adapted to the function and rhythm of its position. The modular logic allows different copies of the same product to coexist while adapting to the functions and tempos of the environment.

Separè

The Separè is a fourth element in the Metis system — formally coherent but structurally independent. Unlike the three seating configurations, which share the same base and cushion components, the room divider required an entirely new module developed from scratch.

The module follows the same formal philosophy: its geometry is derived from the Sofable logo, its curves share the language of the base frame. But its construction logic is different — a standalone unit, interlockable with rotations of 90° from each adjacent module, generating a continuous pattern inspired by chainmail. The result is a sculptural structure that extends vertically across the full height of a wall with rhythm and fluidity.
